name: Vocabulary Growth Rate
description: Analyzes the mathematical rate at which novel (previously unused) words are introduced as a document progresses. According to Heaps' Law, human vocabulary growth follows an unpredictable curve characterized by sudden bursts (when a new subtopic is introduced) and long plateaus. Human writers introduce new terminology in clusters driven by narrative necessity. Conversely, Large Language Models—optimized for consistent token generation and steady perplexity bounds—tend to distribute the introduction of new vocabulary at a mathematically smooth, highly predictable rate. An AI will rarely exhaust its vocabulary early, nor will it suddenly dump an overwhelming number of novel terms late in a text.
algorithm: Heaps' Law Deviation & Log-Linear Growth Profiling
mechanism: The algorithm processes the text sequentially, plotting the cumulative number of unique tokens ($V$) against the total number of processed tokens ($N$). It calculates the exponent $\beta$ in Heaps' law ($V = k N^\beta$) and measures the variance/residuals of the actual text curve against an idealized logarithmic curve. A vocabulary growth curve that is 'too perfect'—showing minimal deviation from a smooth logarithmic trajectory, lacking the organic bursts and plateaus indicative of human cognitive shifts—yields a high artificiality score.
useCase: Highly effective for analyzing mid-to-long form content (essays, reports, articles) where the macroscopic pacing of vocabulary introduction becomes statistically significant.
strengths:
• Exploits a fundamental trait of autoregressive generation: the LLM's inherent drive to maintain a steady probability distribution across the entire output window, preventing natural semantic clustering.
• Extremely difficult to bypass using standard prompting, as the user cannot easily dictate the exact mathematical rate at which new words should be introduced.
limitations:
• Entirely ineffective on short texts (like tweets or brief emails) where the vocabulary growth curve has not had enough tokens to stabilize or show meaningful divergence.
• Highly structured, formulaic human writing (like legal contracts or standard operating procedures) may naturally exhibit a smoothed, AI-like vocabulary growth rate.
parameters:
Analysis: Sequential Token Accumulation Tracking
Metric: Variance from Idealized Heaps' Law Model
Output: 0-100 Growth Rate Artificiality Score
accuracy: Moderate to High — 70-85% accuracy. Its predictive power scales directly with document length. Best used as a macroscopic structural metric in conjunction with localized syntactic checks.

references.title: Herdagdelen, A. et al. (2016). The mathematical formulation of Heaps' law. PLOS ONE.
Tulchinskii, E. et al. (2023). Intrinsic Dimension of Data Representations in Deep Neural Networks. NeurIPS.
